html:
Lower grades do not end your university plan.

Some UK universities with low entry requirements offer undergraduate courses or foundation year routes for students with around 72–96 UCAS points. If you have CCC, CDD or DDD at A-Level, you may still have realistic options through selected degrees, contextual offers, Clearing or portfolio-based admissions, depending on the course and your eligibility.

Here’s the thing. “Low entry requirements” does not mean poor teaching, weak degrees or an easy course. It usually means the university considers more than one set of grades and assesses whether you have the qualifications, skills and preparation needed to succeed.

This guide explains what low entry requirements mean, which UK universities may suit students with lower grades, how UCAS points work, and what to check before applying. If you are still planning your wider route, start with a realistic UK degree plan before choosing courses.

Quick Answer: What Counts as Low Entry Requirements in the UK?

A course can be considered low-entry if it asks for roughly 96 UCAS points or fewer, or if it offers a foundation route for students below standard first-year entry.

UCAS explains that entry requirements can include grades, UCAS Tariff points, specific subjects, interviews, admissions tests, portfolios or other evidence of suitability. That means the exact course page matters more than the university name.

Should You Apply Now or Prepare for the Next Intake?

Your best route depends on timing, qualifications and course availability.

If you are applying late in the current cycle, focus on courses still accepting applications, Clearing where available, direct university contact and foundation year routes. Speed matters, but rushed choices can still hurt you. Check the application dates published by UCAS before making a decision.

If you are preparing for the next intake, you have more time. Use it to compare courses, entry requirements, scholarship options, English language rules, personal statement requirements and location. For 2027 entry, the main UCAS equal-consideration deadline is 13 January 2027, although some courses have an earlier deadline.

The short answer is simple: late applicants need to check available options promptly; early applicants have more time to build a stronger application strategy.

Top UK Universities with Low Entry Requirements

This is not a league table. These universities are included because they are often considered by students looking for accessible entry, foundation years, flexible admissions, practical courses or portfolio-based routes.

Important: the UCAS points mentioned below are examples from selected courses, not university-wide entry requirements. A university may accept lower grades for a foundation year and ask for higher grades for direct entry. Always check the latest official course page, including subject-specific conditions, before applying.

1. London Metropolitan University

London Metropolitan University is one of the strongest examples for accessible UK study routes. Some courses have relatively low UCAS requirements, while selected foundation year options consider students with fewer points than standard first-year entry.

Typical route: Foundation year, selected undergraduate courses or Clearing

Entry example: Computer Science (including foundation year) accepts a minimum of 32 UCAS points from an appropriate Level 3 qualification, or at least one A-Level, alongside specified GCSE requirements.

Best for: Business, computing, architecture, social sciences and creative subjects

London gives students access to employers, events and work experience. It also costs more to live there. That part matters. A lower entry requirement is only helpful if the full budget still works. Check the university's published conditions for a computing foundation route when comparing similar courses.

2. University of Roehampton

Roehampton can suit students who want a London university with a campus feel. Some courses are selective, but foundation and contextual routes may create extra flexibility.

Typical route: Foundation year, contextual offer or Clearing

Entry example: For 2027 entry, BSc Digital Business Management lists 96–112 UCAS points for direct entry and 64–80 points for its foundation year route.

Best for: Education, business, psychology, humanities and social sciences

Do not judge Roehampton only by acceptance-rate claims online. A university can be flexible in one subject and competitive in another. The entry conditions for its Digital Business Management degree provide a useful example of how foundation requirements differ from direct entry.

3. Lincoln Bishop University (Formerly Bishop Grosseteste University)

Lincoln Bishop University, previously known as Bishop Grosseteste University, is based in Lincoln and is often considered by students interested in education, childhood studies and teaching-related subjects. Its smaller academic environment may appeal to students who prefer closer academic support.

Typical route: Selected undergraduate courses or foundation year programmes

Entry example: Education Studies normally requires 96 UCAS points, while its foundation year route has no formal UCAS points requirement, although other academic and progression conditions apply.

Best for: Education, childhood studies, humanities and social sciences

A smaller university is not a downgrade. For some students, it is exactly what helps them settle, ask questions and build confidence. The university explains the different conditions for applicants considering an Education Studies foundation year.

4. Buckinghamshire New University

Buckinghamshire New University focuses on practical, career-based teaching. It can be a good match for students who want applied learning rather than a purely academic course.

Typical route: Foundation year or practical course entry

Entry example: Some previously published courses have listed 88–112 UCAS points for direct entry and 32–56 points for a foundation year. Requirements must be checked for the intended intake.

Best for: Business, aviation, creative industries, computing and health-related subjects

Look carefully at assessment style. A coursework-heavy course may suit one student better than an exam-heavy course, even if the entry requirement looks similar. Some creative and practical programmes may also assess applicants through interviews, auditions or relevant experience.

5. University of Bedfordshire

The University of Bedfordshire is frequently considered by students looking for flexible entry routes. Its campuses in Luton, Bedford, Milton Keynes and Aylesbury also give students more location choice.

Typical route: Foundation year, flexible entry or consideration of relevant experience

Entry example: Aviation and Airport Management lists 96 UCAS points for standard entry and 48 points for its foundation route, subject to additional qualification requirements.

Best for: Business, computing, media, sport, health and education

Bedfordshire can be useful for students whose grades do not show their full ability. Relevant work experience, a focused personal statement and a realistic course choice can strengthen an application where the university considers such evidence.

6. Anglia Ruskin University

Anglia Ruskin University offers a wide course range across locations such as Cambridge, Chelmsford and Peterborough, with additional options at ARU London. Some routes are accessible, particularly through foundation or pathway-style study.

Typical route: Foundation or pathway route

Entry example: Supply Chain Management and International Business lists 96–112 UCAS points for standard entry. Its foundation route uses separate qualification conditions rather than the same tariff range.

Best for: Business, computing, healthcare, engineering and creative subjects

For international applicants, English requirements can matter as much as grades. Before applying, check which English language conditions apply to your preferred university course. Entry requirements can also differ between ARU campuses and programmes.

7. University of Wolverhampton

The University of Wolverhampton is a practical option for students looking for career-focused study and foundation routes. It is often considered for courses linked to employability and professional skills.

Typical route: Foundation year or selected undergraduate entry

Entry example: Architecture with Foundation Year lists 48 UCAS points for 2027 entry and also describes an alternative assessment pathway for some applicants below that level.

Best for: Engineering, business, health, education and computing

One overlooked benefit is cost. Living outside London may reduce pressure, especially during the first year when students are still adjusting to university life. The published Architecture foundation entry conditions show why checking the specific route matters.

8. Aberystwyth University

Aberystwyth University may not always have the lowest UCAS points for direct entry, but it can still suit students looking for a supportive university environment and course-specific flexibility.

Typical route: Integrated foundation year, course-specific entry or international foundation options

Entry example: Many standard undergraduate courses ask for around 104–128 UCAS points, while selected foundation year programmes, including Law with Foundation Year, list 48 points in the university's 2027 prospectus.

Best for: Environmental science, politics, geography, agriculture and humanities

Aberystwyth offers a quieter setting than major city universities. Some students do better in that environment. Fewer distractions can help. Compare the individual courses in the university's published undergraduate prospectus rather than assuming that all degrees share the same tariff.

9. Ravensbourne University London

Ravensbourne University London is a specialist creative university. It is highly relevant for students whose strongest evidence is creative work rather than exam results.

Typical route: Portfolio-based assessment or creative foundation route

Entry example: BA (Hons) Fashion lists 64 UCAS points and a portfolio or showreel requirement for September 2027 entry.

Best for: Design, fashion, media, animation, digital technology and creative industries

This is where grades may not tell the full story. A strong portfolio can sometimes do more than an extra grade, but it does not automatically replace mandatory academic requirements. Applicants can compare the details in the university's 2027 undergraduate prospectus.

10. Arts University Plymouth

Arts University Plymouth, formerly Plymouth College of Art, suits students interested in art, design, photography, illustration, craft and creative practice.

Typical route: Portfolio-based admissions or foundation preparation

Entry example: BA (Hons) Fine Art typically lists 104–120 UCAS points, with creative suitability considered as part of the admissions process.

Best for: Art, design, photography, illustration and creative media

For creative courses, show process. Sketches, experiments and development work can be just as important as polished final pieces. The university's Fine Art course information provides more detail on its degree and extended-study options.

These figures are indicative, not guarantees. Universities may change requirements by course, applicant background, interview, portfolio, English level and available places. Always verify the specific programme and intake on the university's official website.

Can You Get into University with CCC, CDD or DDD?

Yes, but your route should match your grades.

With CCC, you have around 96 UCAS points. That can be enough for selected undergraduate courses and many foundation years.

With CDD, you have around 80 UCAS points. Foundation years, contextual offers and Clearing become more important.

With DDD, you have around 72 UCAS points. Direct entry may be limited, but foundation routes can still work.

Think about it this way: applying only to courses above your grade range is risky. A stronger plan includes one ambitious choice, two realistic choices and two safer choices. Before you submit, make sure you understand how UCAS applications work, because small mistakes can cost you good options.

Low Entry Requirements vs High Acceptance Rate

This is where many students get confused.

A low entry requirement means the course asks for fewer grades or UCAS points. A high offer rate means a university makes offers to a relatively large proportion of applicants, while an acceptance rate generally refers to applicants who secure a place. They are related, but they are not the same.

A university may make offers to many business applicants but still ask for higher grades in nursing. Another university may consider creative students with lower grades but expect a strong portfolio. Course-specific admission conditions matter more than general acceptance-rate claims.

So ask three questions before choosing a course:

  • What UCAS points does the exact course ask for?
  • Does it offer a foundation year?
  • Does it accept evidence beyond grades?

That gives you a clearer answer than acceptance rate alone.

Foundation Years for Students with Lower Grades

A foundation year is an extra year before Year 1 of a degree. It helps students build subject knowledge, academic writing, research skills and confidence.

Foundation years can suit students who missed expected grades, changed subject direction, studied a different curriculum, have a study gap or need more preparation before degree-level work.

In England, the standard full-time undergraduate tuition fee cap for eligible home-fee students at qualifying providers is £9,790 for 2026/27 and £10,050 for 2027/28. Some classroom-based foundation years have a lower fee cap of £5,760, while other foundation programmes may be charged at the applicable standard undergraduate rate. These amounts do not apply to every provider, student fee category or UK nation. Check the government's published tuition fee information alongside the university's own fee page before applying.

For international students, foundation year tuition fees vary by university, course and provider. Around £10,000–£18,000 may be a useful starting point for comparing selected programmes, but it is not a fixed UK-wide range. London, lab-based, specialist and international pathway courses may cost more, and 2027 fees should be checked individually.

Contextual Offers

Contextual admissions allow universities to look at your background, not just your grades. UCAS explains that contextual admissions may lead universities to consider personal circumstances and, where appropriate, adjust their usual offer so students get a fair chance to access their chosen course.

You may be considered if you come from a low-participation area, have been in care, faced disruption, qualify for widening access criteria or meet other university-specific rules. Eligibility varies between institutions and courses, and some contextual offer schemes are intended primarily for UK applicants rather than all international students.

The important part: contextual offers can lower entry requirements for eligible applicants, but they do not remove academic standards or guarantee admission. You still need to show you can manage the course. Check the official UCAS explanation of contextual admissions and the university's own eligibility rules before assuming you qualify.

Clearing with Low Grades

Clearing can help if your grades are lower than expected, you apply late, change your mind or hold no offers. However, course availability and entry requirements vary, and not every university programme will have places.

Prepare before you need it. Keep your UCAS ID, grades, course interests and a short explanation ready. Search available courses, check foundation routes and contact universities directly when places appear. The official UCAS Clearing guidance explains how to explore available options.

For example, a student with CDD who wants business management may miss their first choice but still find a foundation year with available places. Contacting the university promptly can help them understand the available routes and admission conditions, although it does not guarantee an offer.

Online forms are useful. A direct call can still matter.

Preparing Early for the Next Intake

Early preparation gives you more control.

Use the extra time to compare course requirements, foundation options, scholarship availability, English language rules, personal statement expectations and location. Do not build your list only around “easy entry”. Build it around fit.

A sensible shortlist for a standard undergraduate UCAS application can include:

  • one ambitious course
  • two realistic courses
  • two safer courses
  • at least one suitable foundation route within those five choices if your grades are low
  • one backup option outside your preferred city, included within your available choices

For 2027 entry, applicants can normally select up to five undergraduate course choices through UCAS. The personal statement follows the three-question format introduced for 2026 entry, covering subject interest, academic preparation and relevant experiences beyond education. You can review UCAS guidance on preparing your personal statement before finalising your application.

This approach gives you more control and less panic later.

Alternative Routes if Your Grades Are Too Low

If your grades are below the usual foundation range, consider an Access to HE Diploma, especially if you are a mature learner. QAA describes Access to HE as a route for people who want to study at university but do not have traditional qualifications.

Other options include retaking A-Levels, vocational qualifications, foundation diplomas, degree apprenticeships, portfolio-based creative entry and adult learner routes.

Students returning to education after a break may also want to explore routes for mature or non-traditional applicants.

International Students with Low Grades

International students can apply with lower grades, but the right route depends on country, qualification, English level and course choice. UK universities may assess international qualifications differently from A-Levels, so applicants should check the academic requirements for their country and intended programme.

Common routes include:

  • international foundation year
  • undergraduate pathway programme
  • direct entry with lower academic conditions
  • English preparation course
  • pre-master's course for students preparing for postgraduate study

An international foundation year or undergraduate pathway may help students prepare for bachelor's degree entry. A pre-master's course serves a different purpose and is generally intended for applicants progressing towards a master's degree.

Do Low-Entry Universities Offer Good Employability?

They can.

Employability depends on the course, placement options, location, portfolio, work experience and how active the student is. Entry grades open the door. They do not build the career.

A student with lower A-Level grades who chooses a practical course, completes a placement and builds evidence of skills can do very well. A student at a more selective university who does nothing beyond lectures may struggle.

Look for placement years, employer projects, professional accreditation, strong careers support, portfolio opportunities and clear graduate outcomes data.

That is the more useful test.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which UK universities accept 72 UCAS points?

Some UK universities offer foundation year courses with entry requirements at or below 72 UCAS points. Selected routes at the University of Wolverhampton and University of Roehampton provide examples of lower-tariff entry. Options depend on the exact course, additional qualifications, applicant background and available places.

Is 96 UCAS points enough for university?

Yes. 96 UCAS points, roughly CCC at A-Level, can be enough for selected undergraduate courses and many foundation routes. However, applicants must also meet any course-specific subject, GCSE or additional entry requirements.

Can I still apply late with low grades?

Yes, but your realistic route may be Clearing, direct university contact or a foundation year with available places. Act promptly, check the relevant UCAS deadlines and confirm course availability.

Should I wait for the next intake instead?

If you are not ready, do not rush into the wrong course. Waiting for the next intake may give you more time to improve your application, compare universities and review tuition fees, scholarships and living costs.

Can I get into university with CDD?

Yes, but foundation years, Clearing and contextual offers may be more realistic than highly competitive direct-entry courses. The available options depend on your qualifications and the specific university.

Can I get into university with DDD?

Yes, in some cases. DDD gives around 72 UCAS points, which can work for certain foundation or pathway routes, subject to additional entry conditions.

Are foundation years easier to get into?

They often have lower entry requirements than direct Year 1 entry. They are not easy, though. They prepare you for degree-level work, and students must meet the university's progression requirements.

Is a high acceptance rate the same as low entry requirements?

No. Acceptance rates generally relate to applicants who secure places, while offer rates measure offers made to applicants. Entry requirements describe the grades, UCAS points or qualifications a course asks for.

Final Word

Universities with low entry requirements give students another route into higher education. Not a shortcut. Not a weaker future. A different route.

If you are applying late, move quickly and focus on Clearing, foundation routes and available places. If you are preparing for the next intake, use the time well. Build a balanced shortlist, match your UCAS points to the right route, and avoid applying randomly.

Lower grades may change your path.

They do not have to end it.
